channel.title: World
channel.description: The Washington Post World section provides information and analysis of breaking world news stories. In addition to our world news and video, Post World News offers discussions and blogs on major international news and economic issues.

item.title: They went to Nepal for a spiritual journey. Then an epic flood arrived.
item.dc:creator: Amy B Wang, Liam Bowman, Violet Jira
item.description: At least 85 U.S. citizens remain missing in Nepal and Tibet after a glacier collapse caused devastating floods.

item.title: U.S. forces strike Iranian launch site in first disclosed attack in nearly a month
item.dc:creator: Alex Horton
item.description: The U.S. struck Iranian launchers on an island in the Strait of Hormuz, the first publicly acknowledged attack on Tehran’s forces in weeks.

item.title: Ontario’s premier urges thaw in U.S.-Canada trade war: ‘We’re best friends.’
item.dc:creator: Sammy Westfall
item.description: After days of trading insults with President Donald Trump, Ontario Premier Doug Ford said it was vital for the American and Canadian economies that the countries strike a trade deal.

item.title: Military leaders warn Hegseth against extending Iran war operations
item.dc:creator: Alex Horton, Tara Copp
item.description: A recent classified assessment advised that prolonged large-scale operations in the Middle East risk weakening U.S. capabilities elsewhere.

item.title: Venezuela vowed not to ‘hand over’ its oil. Trump aims to grab a windfall.
item.dc:creator: Samantha Schmidt, Helena Carpio
item.description: The deal cements the United States’ long-term dominance over Venezuela, which has become a neo-colony since the U.S. military’s capture of then-President Nicolás Maduro in January.

item.title: Trump’s ambassador to Italy is flaunting his wealth, and it’s dividing Italians
item.dc:creator: Anthony Faiola
item.description: With a net worth of $11.1 billion, Tilman Fertitta, a great-grandson of Sicilian immigrants, is one of the wealthiest people ever to be a U.S. ambassador.

item.title: Russian strikes on food warehouses pose threat of shortages in Ukraine
item.dc:creator: Anastacia Galouchka
item.description: Moscow has shifted to targeting shopping centers and food distribution sites, and markets in Kyiv and other cities are struggling to keep their shelves stocked.

item.title: An aging population in China inspires a new industry: Adult children for hire
item.dc:creator: Huiyee Chiew, Lyric Li
item.description: A low fertility rate and a rapidly aging population have swelled the number of lonely seniors. Young companion workers and start-ups are stepping in to help.

item.title: Beijing expands purge of top generals
item.dc:creator: Joshua Yang
item.description: President Xi Jinping is targeting officers affiliated with previously ousted leaders, analysts say, even as Beijing seeks to project power across the Indo-Pacific.

item.title: Sliman Mansour has died. His art became a symbol of Palestinian resilience.
item.dc:creator: Harrison Smith
item.description: For more than 50 years, he explored Palestinian life and history in his paintings. His work became increasingly political after he spent time in jail.

item.title: Ka-nyet! Kanye West concerts canceled in Russia.
item.dc:creator: Mary Ilyushina
item.description: Two sold-out shows in St. Petersburg were scrapped, highlighting wartime ambivalence about Western culture and the rapper’s past antisemitic remarks.
